questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Regulating Act of 1773? 1️⃣ It designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of India'. 2️⃣ It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta. 3️⃣ It prohibited the servants of the Company from engaging in any private trade.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because it designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal', not India. Lord Warren Hastings was the first such Governor-General. Statement 2 is correct as it established the Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774. Statement 3 is correct as it prohibited private trade and bribery.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Pitt's India Act of 1784 — 1️⃣ It established a system of double government. 2️⃣ It created the Board of Control to manage political affairs. 3️⃣ The Company's territories were called 'British possessions in India' for the first time.
questions.e: All statements are correct . The Act distinguished between commercial and political functions, allowing the Court of Directors to manage commercial affairs while the Board of Control managed political affairs, thus creating double government . It also termed Company territories as 'British possessions'.

questions.q: With reference to the Charter Act of 1833, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It made the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India. 2️⃣ It ended the activities of the East India Company as a commercial body. 3️⃣ It introduced a system of open competition for the selection of civil servants.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are correct. Lord William Bentick was the first Governor-General of India. Statement 3 is incorrect because while it *attempted* to introduce open competition, the provision was negated after opposition from the Court of Directors.

questions.q: The 'Portfolio system', which gave recognition to the administrative departments, was introduced by:
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 gave recognition to the 'portfolio' system, which had been introduced by Lord Canning in 1859. Under this, a member of the Viceroy's council was made in-charge of one or more departments.

questions.q: Which Act is known as the 'Morley-Minto Reforms'?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as Morley-Minto Reforms, named after Lord Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy).

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act of 1919 — 1️⃣ It introduced dyarchy at the provincial level. 2️⃣ It introduced bicameralism and direct elections for the first time. 3️⃣ It provided for the establishment of a public service commission.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act divided provincial subjects into transferred and reserved (dyarchy) . It replaced the Indian Legislative Council with a bicameral legislature (Council of State and Legislative Assembly). It also led to the setting up of the Central Public Service Commission in 1926.

questions.q: With reference to the Government of India Act of 1935, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation. 2️⃣ It abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced 'provincial autonomy'. 3️⃣ It provided for the adoption of dyarchy at the Centre.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act aimed to establish a federation of provinces and princely states. It abolished provincial dyarchy, granting provinces autonomous status. It also provided for dyarchy at the Centre, though this provision never came into operation.

questions.q: Which Act abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India?
questions.e: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India and transferred its functions to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly — 1️⃣ It was a fully sovereign body created by the Indian Independence Act of 1947. 2️⃣ It acted as both a constituent body and a legislative body. 3️⃣ When it met as a legislative body, it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because when the Assembly met as a legislative body (the first Parliament), it was chaired by G.V. Mavlankar. Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired it only when it met as a constituent body.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the most important committee, the Drafting Committee, set up on August 29, 1947.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Union Powers Committee: Jawaharlal Nehru 2️⃣ Provincial Constitution Committee: Sardar Patel 3️⃣ Steering Committee: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
questions.e: All pairs are correctly matched. Union Powers Committee was headed by Nehru , Provincial Constitution Committee by Sardar Patel , and Steering Committee by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

questions.q: With reference to the Preamble, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is based on the 'Objectives Resolution' moved by Pandit Nehru. 2️⃣ It has been amended only once, adding the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'. 3️⃣ It is a source of power to the legislature and can be enforced in courts.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Preamble is neither a source of power to the legislature nor is it justiciable (enforceable in courts).

questions.q: The concept of 'Procedure Established by Law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from:
questions.e: The 'Procedure Established by Law' (found in Article 21) was borrowed from the Japanese Constitution.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 1 of the Constitution — 1️⃣ It describes India as a 'Union of States'. 2️⃣ The phrase 'Union of States' implies that states have no right to secede. 3️⃣ 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than 'Union of India'.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 1 uses 'Union of States'. Dr. Ambedkar noted this implies the Indian Federation is not an agreement and states cannot secede. 'Territory of India' includes states, UTs, and acquired territories, while 'Union of India' includes only states.

questions.q: The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act (2015) is related to:
o: Constitutional status to National Commission for Backward Classes
questions.e: The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act (2015) was enacted to give effect to the land boundary agreement and exchange of enclaves between India and Bangladesh.

questions.q: Which Commission recommended the reorganization of states on the basis of 'administrative convenience' rather than linguistic factor?
questions.e: The Dhar Commission (Linguistic Provinces Commission, 1948) recommended reorganization based on administrative convenience.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Citizenship in India — 1️⃣ The Constitution contains permanent and elaborate provisions for citizenship. 2️⃣ Only a citizen by birth is eligible for the office of President in India. 3️⃣ Fundamental Rights under Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available only to citizens.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; the Constitution only identifies who became citizens at its commencement (Articles 5-11) and leaves subsequent acquisition/loss to Parliament . Statement 2 is incorrect; in India, both citizens by birth and naturalized citizens are eligible for the Presidency (unlike the USA). Statement 3 is correct; these specific rights are denied to aliens .

questions.q: Article 13 of the Indian Constitution is important because — 1️⃣ It expressively provides for the doctrine of judicial review. 2️⃣ It declares all laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights as void. 3️⃣ It includes non-legislative sources like custom or usage in the definition of 'law'.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 13 provides the basis for judicial review. It voids inconsistent laws. Its wide connotation of 'law' includes permanent laws, ordinances, statutory instruments, and customs .

questions.q: Which of the following are exceptions to the Right to Equality (Article 14)? 1️⃣ The President of India and state Governors enjoy immunity from criminal proceedings. 2️⃣ Foreign sovereigns, ambassadors, and diplomats enjoy immunity from civil and criminal proceedings. 3️⃣ Laws made for implementing certain Directive Principles (Article 39b and 39c).
questions.e: All are correct exceptions. Article 361 provides immunities to the President and Governors. Foreign diplomats have immunity. Article 31-C protects laws implementing Article 39(b) or (c) from being challenged under Article 14.

questions.q: With reference to Article 15, consider the following — 1️⃣ It prohibits discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. 2️⃣ It allows the state to make special provisions for women and children. 3️⃣ The 103rd Amendment Act (2019) added reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS).
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 15(1) uses 'only' to specify prohibited grounds. 15(3) allows special provisions for women and children. 15(6) for EWS was added by the 103rd Amendment.

questions.q: Which Supreme Court case is popularly known as the 'Mandal case'?
o: Minerva Mills vs. Union of India
Golak Nath vs. State of Punjab
Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
questions.e: The Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India (1992) case is also called the Mandal case.

questions.q: The 'Creamy Layer' exclusion for OBCs was first identified by which committee?
questions.e: The Ram Nandan Committee was appointed to identify the creamy layer among the OBCs following the Indra Sawhney ruling.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Abolition of Untouchability — 1️⃣ Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. 2️⃣ The term 'untouchability' is defined in the Constitution. 3️⃣ The right under Article 17 is available against private individuals.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution or the Protection of Civil Rights Act.

questions.q: With reference to Article 19, which of the following is NOT one of the six guaranteed rights?
o: Right to form associations or unions
Right to move freely throughout the territory of India
Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property
Right to freedom of speech and expression
questions.e: The right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property was originally the 7th right in Article 19 but was omitted by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 20 — 1️⃣ It protects against ex-post-facto laws in both civil and criminal matters. 2️⃣ It provides protection against 'Double Jeopardy'. 3️⃣ The protection against self-incrimination does not extend to blood specimens.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because the limitation on ex-post-facto laws applies only to criminal laws, not civil or tax laws. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Self-incrimination protection excludes compulsory thumb impressions, signatures, or blood specimens.

questions.q: Which Supreme Court case introduced the concept of 'Due Process of Law' into Article 21?
questions.e: In the Maneka case (1978), the Supreme Court introduced the American expression 'due process of law' by ruling that the procedure established by law must be reasonable, fair, and just.

questions.q: Article 21-A, which makes elementary education a Fundamental Right, was added by:
questions.e: Article 21-A was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002.

questions.q: With reference to Preventive Detention (Article 22), consider the following: 1️⃣ It means detention of a person without trial and conviction by a court. 2️⃣ The detention cannot exceed three months unless an advisory board reports sufficient cause. 3️⃣ Grounds of detention must always be disclosed, even if against public interest.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because facts considered against public interest need not be disclosed to the detenu.

questions.q: Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits: 1️⃣ Begar and other similar forms of forced labour. 2️⃣ Traffic in human beings, including prostitution. 3️⃣ Employment of children in hazardous industries.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are covered under Article 23. Statement 3 is incorrect because the prohibition of child employment is covered under Article 24, not Article 23.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Right to Freedom of Religion — 1️⃣ Article 25 covers both religious beliefs (doctrines) and religious practices (rituals). 2️⃣ The right to propagate religion includes the right to convert another person. 3️⃣ Wearing and carrying of 'kirpans' is included in the profession of the Sikh religion.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the right to propagate does not include a right to convert another person, as forcible conversions impinge on the freedom of conscience.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are correct regarding the Writ of Mandamus? 1️⃣ It is a command issued to a public official to perform failed duties. 2️⃣ It can be issued against a private individual. 3️⃣ it cannot be issued against the President of India or state Governors.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as Mandamus *cannot* be issued against a private individual or body.

questions.q: The Writ of 'Quo-Warranto' can be sought by:
questions.e: Unlike other writs, Quo-Warranto can be sought by any public-minded person and not necessarily by the aggrieved person.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 33 — 1️⃣ It empowers Parliament to restrict Fundamental Rights of armed forces. 2️⃣ This power is available to both Parliament and State Legislatures. 3️⃣ Laws made under Article 33 cannot be challenged for violating Fundamental Rights.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the power to make laws under Article 33 is conferred *only* on Parliament.

questions.q: With reference to 'Martial Law' and 'National Emergency', which is correct? 1️⃣ Martial Law affects only Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ National Emergency suspends the government and ordinary law courts. 3️⃣ Martial Law is imposed to restore law and order after breakdown.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because National Emergency *continues* the government and ordinary law courts, whereas Martial Law suspends them.

questions.q: According to Article 35, the power to prescribe punishment for 'untouchability' (Article 17) vests in:
questions.e: Article 35 lays down that the power to make laws for prescribing punishment for offences like untouchability vests *only* in the Parliament to ensure uniformity across India.

questions.q: The Right to Property was abolished as a Fundamental Right by:
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 abolished the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right. It is now a legal right under Article 300-A.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Basic Structure' doctrine — 1️⃣ It was established by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973). 2️⃣ It limits the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution under Article 368. 3️⃣ Judicial Review is considered a part of the basic structure.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Kesavananda case ruled Parliament cannot alter the 'basic structure'. The I.R. Coelho case reaffirmed that judicial review is a 'basic feature'.

questions.q: Which Article is described by Dr. Ambedkar as the 'soul of the Constitution'?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the most important article, the 'very soul' and 'very heart' of the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to 'Exceptions to Fundamental Rights', consider the following: 1️⃣ Article 31-A saves laws providing for acquisition of estates. 2️⃣ Article 31-B immunizes laws included in the Ninth Schedule from all Fundamental Rights. 3️⃣ Article 31-C protects laws giving effect to certain Directive Principles.
questions.e: All are correct exceptions.

questions.q: In the context of Minority Rights (Article 30), which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ The term 'minority' is defined in the Constitution. 2️⃣ It includes both religious and linguistic minorities. 3️⃣ The right to establish institutions is absolute and excludes government regulations.
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect; 'minority' is *not* defined in the Constitution. Statement 3 is incorrect; the right is not absolute and is subject to state regulations for standards and academic excellence.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'negative' concept among Fundamental Rights?
o: Equality of opportunity in public employment
questions.e: 'Equality before law' (Article 14) is a negative concept (absence of special privileges), while 'equal protection of laws' is a positive concept.

questions.q: The 'Instrument of Accession' was used for the integration of which princely state?
questions.e: Kashmir was integrated with India by means of the Instrument of Accession (unlike Junagarh which used a referendum and Hyderabad which used police action).

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Experts Committee of the Congress (1946) — 1️⃣ It was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru. 2️⃣ Its role was to prepare material for the Constituent Assembly. 3️⃣ It drafted a resolution that closely resembled the Objectives Resolution.
questions.e: All statements are correct.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are identified as 'independent bodies' by the Constitution? 1️⃣ Election Commission 2️⃣ Comptroller and Auditor-General 3️⃣ Union Public Service Commission 4️⃣ NITI Aayog
questions.e: The Constitution establishes the Election Commission, CAG, and Public Service Commissions as independent bulwarks . NITI Aayog is not mentioned as such a body.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Writ of Certiorari', which is correct? 1️⃣ It is issued to quash an order already passed by a lower court. 2️⃣ It can be issued on grounds of lack of jurisdiction. 3️⃣ Initially, it could not be issued against administrative authorities.
questions.e: All statements are correct.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to join the Viceroy's Executive Council?
questions.e: Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian to join the Viceroy's executive council, appointed as the Law Member under the Act of 1909.

questions.q: The 'White Paper on Constitutional Reforms' eventually led to the enactment of:
questions.e: Following the Simon Commission report and Round Table Conferences, the 'White Paper' recommendations were incorporated into the Act of 1935.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'dyarchy' — 1️⃣ It means 'double rule'. 2️⃣ It was first introduced in the provinces by the Act of 1919. 3️⃣ It was introduced at the Centre by the Act of 1935.
questions.e: All statements are correct.

questions.q: The 'Communal Award' (1932) was announced by:
questions.e: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced the scheme of minority representation known as the Communal Award in 1932.

questions.q: Which schedule of the Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: The Fourth Schedule specifies the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the states and union territories.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Double Government' system introduced by Pitt’s India Act of 1784? 1️⃣ The Court of Directors was to manage the commercial affairs of the Company. 2️⃣ The Board of Control was created to manage the political affairs. 3️⃣ The Board of Control was empowered to supervise all operations of the civil and military government.
questions.e: Pitt’s India Act of 1784 established a system of double government by distinguishing between the commercial and political functions of the Company . It allowed the Court of Directors to manage commercial affairs but created the Board of Control to manage political affairs, including supervising civil and military government operations.

questions.q: With reference to the Charter Act of 1813, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It abolished the trade monopoly of the Company in India for all commodities including tea. 2️⃣ It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company’s territories in India. 3️⃣ It provided for the spread of western education among the inhabitants of British territories.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because while the Act abolished the trade monopoly in general, it continued the Company's monopoly over trade in tea and trade with China . Statements 2 and 3 are correct as the Act asserted Crown sovereignty and provided for the spread of western education.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Charter Act of 1853 — 1️⃣ It separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General’s council for the first time. 2️⃣ It established the Indian (Central) Legislative Council. 3️⃣ It introduced local representation in the Indian Legislative Council.
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1853 was a significant landmark that separated legislative and executive functions. It established a separate legislative council (Central Legislative Council) and introduced local representation by allowing provincial governments to appoint four out of six new members .

questions.q: The office of the 'Secretary of State for India', created by the Government of India Act of 1858, was responsible to:
questions.e: The Government of India Act of 1858 created the office of the Secretary of State for India, who was a member of the British Cabinet and was ultimately responsible to the British Parliament .

questions.q: With reference to the Indian Councils Act of 1861, consider the following: 1️⃣ It initiated the process of decentralisation by restoring legislative powers to Bombay and Madras. 2️⃣ It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances during an emergency. 3️⃣ It gave statutory recognition to the 'portfolio' system.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act restored legislative powers to Bombay and Madras presidencies, reversing the centralisation trend . It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances with a life of six months and recognized the portfolio system introduced by Lord Canning.

questions.q: Which Act for the first time provided for the association of Indians with the executive councils of the Viceroy and Governors?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) provided for the first time for the association of Indians with the executive councils; Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian to join the Viceroy’s executive council as the Law Member .

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act of 1919 — 1️⃣ It divided provincial subjects into 'transferred' and 'reserved'. 2️⃣ Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with the aid of Ministers responsible to the legislative council. 3️⃣ Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and his executive council without being responsible to the legislative council.
questions.e: These features defined the 'dyarchy' system introduced in the provinces by the 1919 Act . Transferred subjects included education and agriculture, while reserved subjects included police and justice .

questions.q: With reference to the Government of India Act of 1935, which of the following is correct?
o: It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
It made the Governor-General responsible to the Federal Legislature.
It combined the three lists of subjects into a single Union List.
questions.e: The 1935 Act provided for the establishment of a Federal Court, which was set up in 1937. It abolished dyarchy in provinces (introducing provincial autonomy) and divided powers into three lists: Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent.

questions.q: The 'Mountbatten Plan' of June 3, 1947, was primarily concerned with:
o: The reorganization of states on a linguistic basis.
The introduction of responsible government in princely states.
The making of the Indian Constitution.
questions.e: Lord Mountbatten put forth the partition plan, known as the Mountbatten Plan, on June 3, 1947, which was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League .

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Objectives Resolution' — 1️⃣ It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly. 2️⃣ It was adopted unanimously by the Assembly on January 22, 1947. 3️⃣ Its modified version forms the Preamble of the present Constitution.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Nehru moved the resolution on December 13, 1946, and it was adopted on January 22, 1947. This resolution laid down the philosophy of the constitutional structure and its modified version is the Preamble.

questions.q: Who was the constitutional advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Sir B.N. Rau was appointed as the constitutional advisor to the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: With reference to the Preamble, the ideals of 'Liberty, Equality and Fraternity' were taken from the:
questions.e: The ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity in the Indian Preamble were taken from the French Revolution (1789–1799).

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Equality before Law' (Article 14) — 1️⃣ It is a concept of British origin. 2️⃣ It connotes the absence of any special privileges in favour of any person. 3️⃣ It is a positive concept compared to the negative concept of 'Equal Protection of Laws'.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct . Statement 3 is incorrect because 'Equality before Law' is a negative concept (absence of privileges), whereas 'Equal Protection of Laws' (of American origin) is a positive concept (equality of treatment).

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits discrimination against any citizen on grounds *only* of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth?
questions.e: Article 15 provides that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on these specific grounds. The use of the word 'only' means discrimination on other grounds is not prohibited .

questions.q: With reference to the 'Creamy Layer' among OBCs, the children of which of the following are excluded from reservation benefits? 1️⃣ Persons holding constitutional posts like Judges of SC and HCs. 2️⃣ Group 'A' / Class I officers of All India Services. 3️⃣ Professionals like doctors, lawyers, and engineers.
questions.e: All these categories belong to the 'creamy layer' as identified by the government . This exclusion was directed by the Supreme Court to ensure that the most advanced sections do not take the quota benefits.

questions.q: Article 16(4-A), which empowers the State to provide for reservation in promotions for SCs and STs, was added by:
questions.e: The 77th Amendment Act of 1995 added Article 16(4-A) to allow reservation in promotions for SCs and STs not adequately represented in services.

questions.q: The 'Carry Forward Rule' for unfilled reserved vacancies, which does not violate the 50% ceiling rule, was established by:
questions.e: The 81st Amendment Act of 2000 added a provision to Article 16 allowing the State to treat unfilled reserved vacancies of a year as a separate class, ending the 50% ceiling for backlog vacancies .

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 — 1️⃣ It was originally the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955. 2️⃣ It was renamed in 1976 to enlarge its scope. 3️⃣ It defines 'untouchability' as the social disabilities imposed by birth in certain castes.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; the term 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution or the Act, though courts have described its historical practice .

questions.q: With reference to the Abolition of Titles (Article 18), which is/are correct? 1️⃣ The State is prohibited from conferring any title except military or academic distinctions. 2️⃣ A citizen of India is prohibited from accepting any title from a foreign state. 3️⃣ National Awards like Bharat Ratna amount to 'titles' within the meaning of Article 18.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; the Supreme Court in the Balaji Raghavan case (1995) ruled that National Awards do not amount to 'titles' but should not be used as suffixes or prefixes .

questions.q: Which of the following grounds can be used to impose reasonable restrictions on the 'Freedom of Speech and Expression' (Article 19)? 1️⃣ Sovereignty and integrity of India 2️⃣ Friendly relations with foreign states 3️⃣ Public order 4️⃣ Decency or morality
questions.e: All these are mentioned as valid grounds for restrictions under Article 19(2).

questions.q: The freedom to form 'Co-operative Societies' was added as a Fundamental Right by the:
questions.e: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 added 'co-operative societies' to the right to form associations or unions under Article 19(1)(c).

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 20 — 1️⃣ Protection against ex-post-facto laws. 2️⃣ Protection against double jeopardy. 3️⃣ Protection against self-incrimination.
questions.e: Article 20 contains these three specific protections for an accused person .

questions.q: With reference to the 'Right to Education' (Article 21-A), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It provides free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years. 2️⃣ It makes higher and professional education a Fundamental Right. 3️⃣ It was added to the Constitution by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; the right applies only to elementary education, not higher or professional levels.

questions.q: Regarding 'Preventive Detention' in India, which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ The Parliament has exclusive power to make laws for reasons connected with defense and security of India. 2️⃣ State legislatures can never make laws regarding preventive detention. 3️⃣ No other democratic country has made preventive detention an integral part of its Constitution.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; both Parliament and state legislatures can concurrently make such laws for reasons like public order or essential supplies.

questions.q: Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in: 1️⃣ Any factory 2️⃣ Any mine 3️⃣ Hazardous activities like construction 4️⃣ Harmless or innocent work
questions.e: Article 24 prohibits child labor in mines, factories, and hazardous activities but does not prohibit employment in harmless work .

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Freedom of Religion' (Article 25) — 1️⃣ It is available only to the citizens of India. 2️⃣ It is subject to public order, morality, and health. 3️⃣ It covers both religious beliefs and religious practices.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; Article 25 is available to all persons, including non-citizens. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Which Article protects the 'Collective Freedom of Religion' by granting rights to religious denominations?
questions.e: While Article 25 guarantees individual freedom, Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations or their sections to manage their own affairs .

questions.q: Article 27 of the Constitution provides freedom from:
o: Payment of taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.
Discrimination in public employment on religious grounds.
questions.e: Article 27 lays down that no person shall be compelled to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or denomination.

questions.q: With reference to Article 28, in which type of educational institution is religious instruction completely prohibited?
o: Institutions established under an endowment but administered by the State.
Institutions receiving aid from the State.
Institutions wholly maintained by the State.
questions.e: Religious instruction is completely prohibited in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Article 29 — 1️⃣ It provides that any section of citizens has the right to conserve its distinct language, script or culture. 2️⃣ Its protection is restricted *only* to minorities. 3️⃣ It includes the right to agitate for the protection of a language.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; the Supreme Court held that the phrase 'section of citizens' includes both minorities and the majority .

questions.q: Under Article 30, 'Minority Educational Institutions' of which type are subject to the regulatory power of the state regarding syllabus and academic standards? 1️⃣ Institutions that seek recognition and aid. 2️⃣ Institutions that seek recognition but not aid. 3️⃣ Institutions that neither seek recognition nor aid.
questions.e: Types 1 and 2 are subject to state regulatory power regarding academic standards and discipline. Type 3 institutions are free to administer their affairs subject only to general laws like tax and labor laws.

questions.q: Which of the following writs is known as the 'bulwark of individual liberty' against arbitrary detention?
questions.e: The writ of Habeas Corpus ("to have the body of") is a bulwark of liberty as it allows the court to set a person free if their detention is found to be illegal .

questions.q: With reference to the Writ of 'Prohibition', consider the following: 1️⃣ It is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction. 2️⃣ It directs activity, unlike Mandamus which directs inactivity. 3️⃣ It is available against administrative authorities.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; Prohibition directs *inactivity* (to forbid), while Mandamus directs activity. Statement 3 is incorrect; Prohibition is only available against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities .

questions.q: The power to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of the members of armed forces (Article 33) is conferred on:
questions.e: Article 33 empowers the Parliament alone to make such laws to ensure the proper discharge of duties and discipline.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Martial Law' — 1️⃣ It is explicitly defined in the Constitution. 2️⃣ It refers to 'military rule' where civil administration is run by military authorities. 3️⃣ It can be declared in any area within the territory of India under Article 34.
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct . Statement 1 is incorrect; the expression 'martial law' has not been defined anywhere in the Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Viceroy of India' introduced by the Government of India Act of 1858? 1️⃣ He was the direct representative of the British Crown in India. 2️⃣ Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India. 3️⃣ The Viceroy was responsible to the Secretary of State for India.
questions.e: The 1858 Act changed the designation of the Governor-General of India to the Viceroy of India, who acted as the direct representative of the British Crown . Lord Canning was the first to hold this office. The Secretary of State was vested with complete authority over the Indian administration, and the Viceroy reported to this office.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian Councils Act of 1892, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It increased the number of non-official members in the legislative councils. 2️⃣ It gave the councils the power of discussing the budget. 3️⃣ It used the word 'election' for the first time to fill non-official seats.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as the Act increased non-official members and empowered them to discuss the budget and address questions . Statement 3 is incorrect; while it made a limited provision for using recommendations (an indirect form of election), the word 'election' was not actually used in the Act.

questions.q: The 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India is known as:
questions.e: Lord Minto came to be known as the Father of Communal Electorate because the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced a system of communal representation for Muslims by accepting the concept of 'separate electorate'.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act of 1919 — 1️⃣ It required that three of the six members of the Viceroy's executive Council were to be Indian. 2️⃣ It granted franchise to all adults regardless of property or tax. 3️⃣ It separated provincial budgets from the Central budget for the first time.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Act granted franchise to a limited number of people based on property, tax, or other qualifications, rather than universal adult franchise.

questions.q: With reference to the Simon Commission, consider the following: 1️⃣ It was a statutory commission appointed to report on the condition of India under its new Constitution. 2️⃣ All its members were British, leading to a boycott by Indian parties. 3️⃣ It recommended the continuation of dyarchy in the provinces.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct . Statement 3 is incorrect because the commission actually recommended the abolition of dyarchy and the extension of responsible government in the provinces.

questions.q: Which of the following was a feature of the Government of India Act of 1935? 1️⃣ Division of powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent Lists. 2️⃣ Establishment of a Federal Railway Authority. 3️⃣ Separation of Burma (now Myanmar) from India.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act provided for three lists for power division , established the Federal Railway Authority , and separated Burma from India.

questions.q: According to the Indian Independence Act of 1947, who was to appoint the Governor-General for each dominion?
o: The Constituent Assembly of the dominion
questions.e: The Act provided that for each dominion, there would be a Governor-General appointed by the British King on the advice of the dominion cabinet.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Making of the Constitution' — 1️⃣ The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first put forward by M.N. Roy in 1934. 2️⃣ The Assembly was constituted in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. 3️⃣ The seats were allotted in proportion to the respective population of provinces and states.
questions.e: All statements are correct. M.N. Roy proposed the idea in 1934 . The Assembly was formed in November 1946 per the Cabinet Mission Plan , and seats were allotted roughly at one seat per million population .

questions.q: Who was the temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly during its first meeting?
questions.e: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was elected as the temporary Chairman of the Assembly during the first meeting on December 9, 1946, following the French practice .

questions.q: With reference to the 'Changes by the Independence Act' on the Constituent Assembly, consider the following: 1️⃣ The Assembly was made a fully sovereign body. 2️⃣ It could abrogate or alter any law made by the British Parliament in relation to India. 3️⃣ The total strength of the Assembly increased after the withdrawal of the Muslim League.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct . Statement 3 is incorrect because the strength actually came down from 389 to 299 after the Muslim League members from Pakistan areas withdrew .

questions.q: Which of the following functions was NOT performed by the Constituent Assembly?
o: Appointment of the first Prime Minister
Election of the first President of India
Ratification of India's membership of the Commonwealth
questions.e: The Assembly ratified Commonwealth membership, adopted the National Flag, National Anthem, and National Song, and elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President . The Prime Minister (Jawaharlal Nehru) was sworn in by the Governor-General.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Drafting Committee', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ It was set up on August 29, 1947. 2️⃣ It consisted of seven members. 3️⃣ It took more than a year to prepare the first draft.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct . Statement 3 is incorrect because the committee took less than six months (sitting for 141 days) to prepare the draft.

questions.q: On which date did the people of India in the Constituent Assembly 'adopt, enact and give to themselves' the Constitution?
questions.e: November 26, 1949, is the date mentioned in the Preamble as the day the people adopted, enacted, and gave the Constitution to themselves.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Enforcement of the Constitution' — 1️⃣ Major provisions came into force on January 26, 1950. 2️⃣ Provisions relating to citizenship and elections came into force on November 26, 1949. 3️⃣ January 26 was chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj day of 1930.
questions.e: All statements are correct. While some articles (citizenship, elections, etc.) were enforced on Nov 26, 1949, the major part commenced on Jan 26, 1950 . Jan 26 was chosen for its historical significance regarding the 1930 Purna Swaraj celebration .

questions.q: According to the 'Basic Structure' doctrine, the Supreme Court ruled that:
o: The Preamble is not a part of the Constitution and cannot be amended.
The Directive Principles always override Fundamental Rights.
Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution including Fundamental Rights.
Parliament cannot alter the fundamental features that form the basic structure.
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that Article 368 does not enable Parliament to alter the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Salient Features of the Constitution', which is correct? 1️⃣ India has the lengthiest written Constitution in the world. 2️⃣ The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) is known as the 'Mini-Constitution'. 3️⃣ The Constitution provides for a presidential form of government.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because India opted for a British Parliamentary System rather than an American Presidential System.

questions.q: The 'Philosophical part' of the Indian Constitution (Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles) is inspired by:
questions.e: The Fundamental Rights derive inspiration from the American Constitution (Bill of Rights), and the Directive Principles of State Policy from the Irish Constitution.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Federal System with Unitary Bias' — 1️⃣ Supremacy of the Constitution is a federal feature. 2️⃣ Single citizenship is a unitary feature. 3️⃣ The term 'Federation' is explicitly used in Article 1.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct . Statement 3 is incorrect because the term 'Federation' has nowhere been used in the Constitution; Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States' .

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Synthesis of Parliamentary Sovereignty and Judicial Supremacy' in India? 1️⃣ The Supreme Court can declare parliamentary laws unconstitutional. 2️⃣ The Parliament can amend the major portion of the Constitution. 3️⃣ The scope of judicial review in India is wider than in the US.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as the framers preferred a synthesis between British and American principles . Statement 3 is incorrect because the scope of judicial review in India is narrower than in the US due to the 'procedure established by law' vs 'due process of law' .

questions.q: With reference to 'Fundamental Rights' (Part III), consider the following: 1️⃣ They promote the idea of political democracy. 2️⃣ They are justiciable in nature. 3️⃣ They are absolute and not subject to any restrictions.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because Fundamental Rights are not absolute but subject to reasonable restrictions.

questions.q: The 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (Part IV) aim to establish:
questions.e: The Directive Principles are meant for promoting the ideal of social and economic democracy and seek to establish a 'welfare state' in India .

questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of:
questions.e: Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A) were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 based on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.e: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 in 1989 by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Emergency Provisions' — 1️⃣ National emergency is declared under Article 352. 2️⃣ Financial emergency is declared under Article 360. 3️⃣ During emergency, the federal structure converts into a unitary one.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Constitution envisages National, State, and Financial emergencies , which can convert the federal structure into a unitary one without formal amendment.

questions.q: The 'Three-tier Government' (Local Government) was constitutionally recognized by:
questions.e: The 73rd (Panchayats) and 74th (Municipalities) Amendment Acts of 1992 added the third tier of government .

questions.q: With reference to 'Citizenship' (Part II), which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ Friendly aliens enjoy all political rights. 2️⃣ Enemy aliens do not enjoy protection against arrest and detention (Article 22). 3️⃣ Citizens enjoy the right to equality of opportunity in public employment (Article 16).
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; aliens do not enjoy all civil and political rights. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: The 'Single Citizenship' system in India is similar to the system in:
questions.e: The Constitution of India, like that of Canada, has introduced the system of single citizenship, unlike the double citizenship of USA and Australia.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Citizenship Act, 1955' — 1️⃣ It provides for acquisition by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory. 2️⃣ It originally provided for Commonwealth Citizenship. 3️⃣ Commonwealth Citizenship was repealed by the 2003 Amendment Act.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act prescribes five ways of acquisition , and the 2003 Act repealed the recognition of Commonwealth Citizenship .

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way of losing Indian citizenship?
questions.e: The Citizenship Act (1955) prescribes only three ways of losing citizenship: renunciation, termination, and deprivation.

questions.q: The 'Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Cardholder' scheme was created by merging:
questions.e: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2015, introduced the OCI Cardholder scheme by merging the PIO (Person of Indian Origin) card scheme and the OCI card scheme.

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 12', which of the following are included in the definition of 'State'? 1️⃣ Parliament of India 2️⃣ State Legislatures 3️⃣ Municipalities and Panchayats 4️⃣ Statutory authorities like LIC and ONGC
questions.e: Article 12 defines 'State' to include executive/legislative organs of Union and States, all local authorities, and other statutory/non-statutory authorities .

questions.q: The 'Rule of Law' as an element of Article 14 was propounded by:
questions.e: The concept of 'Equality before law' is an element of the 'Rule of Law' propounded by the British jurist A.V. Dicey .

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for 'Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment'?
questions.e: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.

questions.q: The 'Creamy Layer' principle applies to which category of reservation?
questions.e: The Supreme Court directed the government to exclude the 'creamy layer' (advanced sections) among the OBCs while implementing reservation laws.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right is automatically suspended during an external emergency (war or aggression)?
questions.e: The six rights guaranteed by Article 19 are automatically suspended only when an emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Constitution Day' in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is celebrated on November 26 every year. 2️⃣ It was first decided to be celebrated by the Government of India in 2015. 3️⃣ It aims to promote constitutional values among citizens.
questions.e: The Government of India decided in 2015 to celebrate November 26 every year as "Constitution Day" (Samvidhan Divas) to promote constitutional values among citizens. This date marks the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the 'Right to Property'?
o: It is still a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution.
It was made a legal right under Article 300-A by the 44th Amendment Act.
The Supreme Court can directly be moved under Article 32 for its violation.
It is part of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution.
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 abolished the right to property as a Fundamental Right. It is now a legal/constitutional right under Article 300-A in Part XII. Since it is not a Fundamental Right, an aggrieved person cannot directly move the Supreme Court under Article 32.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Constitutionalism' — 1️⃣ A country may have a constitution but not constitutionalism. 2️⃣ It connotes the concept of 'limited government'. 3️⃣ Absolute power in the hands of an individual is a negation of constitutionalism.
questions.e: Constitutionalism means limited government as opposed to arbitrary or total power. A dictatorship may have a constitution (the document) but lacks constitutionalism (the principle of restraint).

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 13', which of the following are included in the wide connotation of 'law'? 1️⃣ Ordinances issued by the President or State Governors. 2️⃣ Custom or usage having the force of law. 3️⃣ Statutory instruments like rules, regulations, or notifications.
questions.e: Article 13 defines 'law' broadly to include permanent laws, temporary laws (ordinances), statutory instruments (delegated legislation), and even non-legislative sources like custom or usage .

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (Committee on the Indian Civil Service), which led to the open competition system, was appointed in:
questions.e: Following the Charter Act of 1853 which introduced an open competition system for civil servants, the Macaulay Committee was appointed in 1854.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Writ of Prohibition' — 1️⃣ It is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding jurisdiction. 2️⃣ It is available against both judicial and administrative authorities. 3️⃣ It is a 'jurisdictional writ' similar to Certiorari.
questions.e: Prohibition is issued to prevent a lower court from exceeding jurisdiction. It is only available against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities, not administrative ones . Like Certiorari, it is a jurisdictional writ but issued at an earlier stage .

questions.q: Under the Indian Independence Act of 1947, the 'Constituent Assembly' had the power to: 1️⃣ Frame and adopt any constitution for the nation. 2️⃣ Repeal any act of the British Parliament, including the Independence Act itself. 3️⃣ Legislate for the respective territories until new constitutions were enforced.
questions.e: The 1947 Act empowered the Assembly to frame any constitution, repeal British laws (including the 1947 Act), and act as a legislature for the dominion .

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of 'Portfolios in the Interim Government (1946)' is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dr. Rajendra Prasad - Food and Agriculture
questions.e: In the Interim Government (1946), Sardar Baldev Singh held the Defence portfolio. Jagjivan Ram was in charge of the Labour portfolio.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Making of the Constitution', the total strength of the Assembly was reduced from 389 to 299 because:
o: The princely states refused to join.
High costs led to a voluntary reduction in members.
The Muslim League members from areas included in Pakistan withdrew.
The British Parliament passed a resolution to limit the size.
questions.e: Following the partition and the withdrawal of Muslim League members hailing from Pakistan, the total strength dropped to 299 .

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made the right to form 'Co-operative Societies' a Fundamental Right?
questions.e: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 made three changes: it created a Fundamental Right to form co-operatives (Article 19), added a new DPSP (Article 43-B), and inserted Part IX-B .

questions.q: Consider the following regarding 'Single Citizenship' in India — 1️⃣ It aims to promote a feeling of fraternity and unity. 2️⃣ Parliament can prescribe residence as a condition for certain employments. 3️⃣ It is a feature borrowed from the Canadian Constitution.
questions.e: India provides single citizenship to promote integration. Parliament has the power under Article 16 to prescribe residence as a qualification for certain jobs. This system is similar to the one in Canada.

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 15', which of the following is an exception to the rule of non-discrimination?
o: Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in educational institutions.
Reservation of seats for women in local bodies.
Special provisions for the advancement of Scheduled Castes.
questions.e: Article 15 allows exceptions for women and children , socially/educationally backward classes or SC/STs , and economically weaker sections.

questions.q: The 'Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill' focuses on:
o: Mandatory vocational training for secondary students.
Primary education infrastructure in rural India.
Granting autonomy to Institutions of National Eminence.
questions.e: The Bill aims to grant full academic, administrative, and financial autonomy to 'Institutions of National Eminence' to help them achieve global excellence.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Drafting Committee' — 1️⃣ It was set up on August 29, 1947. 2️⃣ It consisted of seven members including Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. 3️⃣ The second draft was published in October 1948.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The committee was established in Aug 1947. It had seven members. The second draft followed public comments on the first and was published in Oct 1948.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution is related to 'Abolition of Untouchability'?
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 20', the protection against 'Self-Incrimination' does NOT extend to:
questions.e: The protection against self-incrimination does not extend to the compulsory production of material objects, giving thumb impressions, specimen signatures, or blood specimens.

questions.q: The 'Nowcasting' model mentioned in the Survey is used to:
o: Assess GDP growth in real-time for current quarters.
Monitor the daily fluctuations of the stock market.
questions.e: The Survey introduces a nowcasting model that integrates high-frequency indicators to assess growth in the ongoing and subsequent quarters in real-time.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Preamble' — 1️⃣ It is a part of the Constitution as per the Kesavananda Bharati case. 2️⃣ It was enacted after the rest of the Constitution was already enacted. 3️⃣ It is non-justiciable in nature.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The SC held it is a part of the Constitution in 1973. It was enacted last to ensure conformity with the full text. It is not enforceable in courts.

questions.q: Which mission aims at 100% plastic waste management in urban areas?
questions.e: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan 2.0 specifically targets 100% plastic waste management and scientific landfill processing in all Urban Local Bodies.

questions.q: The 'Critical Minerals Mission' is vital for the manufacturing of:
questions.e: Critical minerals like Lithium and Cobalt are essential components for electric vehicle (EV) batteries and green energy technology.

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 32', consider the following: 1️⃣ It is a Fundamental Right in itself. 2️⃣ It can be used to determine the constitutionality of any law regardless of FR violation. 3️⃣ The Supreme Court's jurisdiction under it is original but not exclusive.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 32 is a Fundamental Right and the SC's jurisdiction is concurrent with High Courts under Article 226 . Statement 2 is incorrect; Article 32 cannot be invoked unless a Fundamental Right is directly infringed .

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to join the Viceroy’s Executive Council as a Law Member?
questions.e: Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's executive council under the Act of 1909 .

questions.q: Regarding 'Preventive Detention' in India, which authority can make laws for reasons connected with the 'Security of a State'?
questions.e: The Parliament has exclusive authority for laws related to defense and foreign affairs, but both Parliament and State Legislatures can concurrently make laws for reasons like the security of a state or public order .

questions.q: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the names of States and Union Territories?
questions.e: The First Schedule contains the names of the States and Union Territories along with their territorial extent.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about 'Article 19' — 1️⃣ It protects six rights available only to citizens. 2️⃣ The rights are available against both state action and private individuals. 3️⃣ The right to strike is a Fundamental Right under Article 19.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct; these rights are denied to foreigners. Statement 2 is incorrect; they are protected *only* against state action. Statement 3 is incorrect; the SC held there is no guaranteed right to strike.

questions.q: 'SASCI' (Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment) loans have a tenure of:
questions.e: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free loans to State governments to support capital expenditure.

questions.q: The 'Regulating Act of 1773' is significant because it:
o: Recognized the commercial functions of the Company for the first time.
Laid the foundations of central administration in India.
questions.e: The Act was a step to control the Company and, for the first time, recognized its political functions and laid the foundations of central administration .

questions.q: With reference to 'Core Inflation', which of the following is correct?
o: It reached a multi-year low of 3.1% in FY26.
It includes the prices of food and fuel.
It is the primary target for the RBI's 4% mandate.
questions.e: Core inflation reached a multi-year low of 3.1% in FY26. It excludes volatile food and fuel components. The RBI's target is headline inflation, not core.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the Parliament to restrict Fundamental Rights of 'Non-combatant' employees of the armed forces, like cooks or tailors?
questions.e: Article 33 applies to members of the armed forces, which the law defines to include non-combatant employees like barbers, cooks, and tailors.

questions.q: The 'Viksit Bharat' vision targets India becoming a developed nation by:
questions.e: 2047 marks the 100th anniversary of Indian independence and is the goal for achieving 'Viksit Bharat' status.

questions.q: Which of the following regulates the 'Account Aggregator' (AA) ecosystem in India?
questions.e: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework, which enables consent-based digital financial data sharing, is under the regulatory purview of the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.q: With reference to 'Union and its Territory', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 1 describes India as a 'Federation of States'. 2️⃣ The name of the country adopted by the Constituent Assembly was 'India, that is, Bharat'. 3️⃣ States have the right to secede from the Indian Union.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; the 'Union' is indestructible and states have no right to secede .

questions.q: The 'Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill' aims to grant autonomy to which category of institutions?
questions.e: The Bill proposes to grant full academic, administrative, and financial autonomy to a new category called 'Institutions of National Eminence' to help them reach global top 100 rankings.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'High-Frequency Indicator' (HFI) used in the DEA's 'Nowcasting' model?
questions.e: The nowcasting model integrates high-frequency indicators like GST collections, power demand, and e-way bills to assess real-time growth for the current quarter.

questions.q: In the context of Fundamental Rights, the term 'State' under Article 12 includes: 1️⃣ Government and Parliament of India 2️⃣ Municipalities and Panchayats 3️⃣ Statutory authorities like LIC and ONGC
questions.e: Article 12 defines 'State' broadly to include the Union and State governments/legislatures, all local authorities, and other statutory or non-statutory authorities .

questions.q: What is the primary objective of the 'PM-JANMAN' mission?
questions.e: PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan) focuses on providing 11 critical interventions for the development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Regulating Act of 1773': 1️⃣ It designated the Governor of Bengal as 'Governor-General of Bengal'. 2️⃣ It established a Supreme Court at Calcutta. 3️⃣ Lord Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General.
questions.e: All statements are correct . The Act was the first step by the British Government to regulate the East India Company and laid the foundations of central administration in India.

questions.q: The concept of 'Due Process of Law' was introduced into Article 21 by the Supreme Court in which case?
questions.e: In the Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India (1978) case, the Supreme Court overruled its earlier narrow view and ruled that the procedure depriving life or liberty must be reasonable, fair, and just, introducing 'due process' .

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.e: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections to 18 years.

questions.q: With reference to 'Economic Complexity Index' (ECI), which of the following is correct?
o: It measures the knowledge intensity of an economy based on export diversity.
It measures the population density of a country.
Lower ECI predicts higher future income.
India's rank has declined over the last decade.
questions.e: ECI measures the knowledge intensity of an economy. India's rank improved from 54 in 2012 to 42 in 2022, and higher complexity is a strong predictor of higher future income.

questions.q: The 'Right to Education' (Article 21-A) provides free and compulsory education to children of which age group?
questions.e: Article 21-A, added by the 86th Amendment, mandates free and compulsory education for children between the ages of six and fourteen years .

questions.q: According to the Economic Survey, what is the 'Viksit Bharat' target year?
questions.e: India aims to achieve the status of a developed nation (Viksit Bharat) by the centenary of its independence in 2047.

questions.q: Which Act for the first time separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General’s council?
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1853 separated these functions and established a separate Indian (Central) Legislative Council .

questions.q: The 'Sovereign Green Bonds' (SGrBs) are primarily used to fund:
o: Green infrastructure and carbon reduction projects
questions.e: SGrBs are issued to mobilize resources for green projects that help India meet its climate commitments and reduce carbon intensity.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency?
questions.e: Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during the operation of a National Emergency.

questions.q: The 'ULIP' portal, which aims to reduce logistics costs, is part of which policy?
questions.e: The Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) is a key digital gateway under the National Logistics Policy.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies is responsible for auditing the accounts of both Central and State governments?
questions.e: The CAG acts as the guardian of the public purse and audits the accounts of both the Union and the State governments .

questions.q: The term 'Strategic Indispensability' in the Survey refers to:
o: Banning all imports from neighboring countries.
Creating a role in global value chains that others cannot easily substitute.
A state where the military runs the economy.
questions.e: Strategic indispensability involves offering critical goods or services to global value chains such that India's role becomes essential and non-substitutable.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the Parliament to restrict the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces?
questions.e: Article 33 allows Parliament to restrict or abrogate the rights of armed forces, police, and intelligence agencies to ensure discipline and proper duty discharge .

questions.q: What is the target production capacity of the 'National Green Hydrogen Mission' by 2030?
questions.e: The mission targets a green hydrogen production capacity of at least 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) per annum by 2030.

questions.q: The 'Preamble' was amended by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
